citations.assessment: The Bavli names both family relationships and describes her exceptional speed of learning.

The passage is at Kelim Metzia 1:3 in this digital edition. It names Beruriah and attributes the specific praise to Rabbi Yehoshua. Heilprin prints chapter 8 and questions the attribution later in the same paragraph.
Rabbi Shimshon quotes the baraita and explicitly preserves Rabbi Yehoshua’s praise. His purity rulings for Rabbi Tarfon and the sages are ordered oppositely to the checked Tosefta and Arukh.
The headword quotes Beruriah’s instruction about moving the lock and the praise attributed to Rabbi Yehoshua.
The linked Chalafta entry quotes the other debate and its praise from Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava.

The cited passage places the daughter’s answer against the son’s and attributes its approval to Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava. It does not name the daughter. The identification and father wording belong to Heilprin’s account.

The checked text gives three hundred teachings from three hundred masters in one day and the three-year contrast in the discussion of Sefer Yuchasin. It does not add “winter,” which Heilprin also uses under Rabbi Meir.
The pointer lands at the beginning of the relevant paragraph under Rabbi Meir.
The expanded account belongs to Rashi’s explanation of a cryptic alternative in the Bavli; the reincarnation explanation is a separate later tradition.
The primary text explicitly identifies Beruriah with Bathsheba, associates the student with Uriah, and links the two deaths. Heilprin’s compressed account follows this version.
The linked paragraph reproduces the Bavli’s alternative and Rashi’s explanation, and repeats Heilprin’s chronological objection.

The statement about the law following her twice remains Heilprin’s inference. The two Tosefta passages give distinct approving statements. They are not, on their own, a later survey of legal codification.
